lemma: Lemma R' analytic part: For any constants beta, c with 0 < beta <= 1 and c >= 1, let n0 = ceil(max(16, 16/beta^2, 2 log2 c / beta)). Then for all n >= n0: 2^(beta n) / (c n) >= n. Proof: the inequality is equivalent to beta n >= log2 c + 2 log2 n. For n >= 2 log2 c / beta, log2 c <= beta n / 2, so it suffices that g(n) = beta n - 4 log2 n >= 0. g is increasing for n >= 4/(beta ln 2), and 16/beta^2 >= 16 >= 4/(beta ln 2) for beta <= 1, so g is increasing on [n0, inf). At n = 16/beta^2, g = 16/beta - 16 + 8 log2 beta >= 0 since 16/beta >= 16 and log2 beta <= 0. Hence g >= 0 on [n0, inf). Scope: beta in (0,1] only; beta > 1 is not covered.

lemma: Lemma FE (finite-exception transfer, per-oracle reading). Fix 0<beta<=1, c>=1, let n0 = n0(beta,c) be the threshold of Lemma R' (R1305), let s(n) = 2^(beta n)/(c n), and define s''(n) = s(n) for n >= n0 and s''(n) = n for n < n0. STATEMENT: (i) s''(n) >= n for every n >= 1; (ii) s'' = s for n >= n0; (iii) if a one-pass algorithm A (for a fixed oracle A) solves search-MCSP^A[s] on all input lengths with space S(n) and update time U(n), then there is a one-pass algorithm A'' for search-MCSP^A[s''] with space max(S(n), K) and update time max(U(n), K) for a constant K = K(beta,c,A) independent of n. PROOF: (i) for n >= n0 this is Lemma R' (2^(beta n)/(cn) >= n); for n < n0 it holds by definition. (ii) by definition. (iii) A'' runs A verbatim for n >= n0. For n < n0 the input has N = 2^n <= 2^(n0) bits, a constant. A'' stores the whole input (constant space) and outputs a fixed answer: the correct search output for threshold n (any valid output if no circuit of size n matches), which depends only on the finitely many pairs (n, truth table) with n < n0 and on the values of A on the finitely many oracle queries those circuits can make. These values are a constant-size advice string that depends on A and beta, c only. Since n0 is constant, K is constant. Hence any lower bound 'no one-pass poly(s'')-space, poly(s'')-update algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s'']' transfers to 'no such algorithm for search-MCSP^A[s]', because for n >= n0 the two thresholds coincide and the additive constant K does not change polynomial bounds. SCOPE: per-oracle reading only (each A gets its own constant advice). If the intended MMW19 statement requires ONE algorithm uniform over all oracles A, the advice step breaks and this is open (new sub-obligation G0003b). Also depends on MMW19 Thm 1.3 being applicable to threshold functions with s(n) >= n for all n (the form in the MMW19 intro), which is not verified at the source (G0001/G0002 remain open).

Suppose a deterministic one-pass algorithm A decides it on every input of length N≥L, using at most S(N) bits of state and at most U(N) work per input bit. The counter uses O(log L) bits. At end of input, the trie branch returns its stored label and the simulation branch returns A's answer. Thus the added state and per-bit work are constants depending only on fixed L.
